name: Near-Rear Logistics Point
representative_system: Generic battalion/regimental near-rear supply point — composite, not a named facility

cost.display: Not a procured unit — a facility/throughput node, not something with a per-unit price

key_facts.label: Function
key_facts.value: Fuel, ammunition and FPV/drone resupply for near-line units

key_facts.label: Movement to line
key_facts.value: Segmented over several days with radio silence during offensive builds

key_facts.label: Typical depth
key_facts.value: Just inside the ~30 km drone-dense corridor either side of the front

short_role: Near-rear point that pushes fuel, ammunition and drone airframes forward to units operating within the drone-dense corridor.
characteristics: Sits inside the ~30 km band either side of the front where persistent drone coverage genuinely dominates
Handles the very high consumption rate of FPV/loitering-munition airframes as well as conventional ammunition
Movement to and from staging is deliberately broken into short guided segments rather than one visible convoy run
employment_notes: Feeds tank and drone units operating close to the line, where a single detected supply run can draw an immediate strike. Consumption here is dominated by FPV airframes rather than artillery shells — a single intensive-tempo drone company can burn through thousands of airframes a month, reshaping what 'resupply' even means compared to a Cold War-era ammunition point.
contrast_vs_traditional: Sitting inside the drone-dense corridor changes what 'near-rear and relatively safe' means — this point is well within the zone where persistent drone coverage dominates, not behind it. That has pushed movement discipline (staggered segments, radio silence, paper orders instead of radio traffic) down to a level that used to only apply to units actually crossing the line.

sources.label: Andrey Markin, 'Summary of Combat Experience of the SVO' — movement/logistics patterns referenced in doctrine reference
